hints.content:
When a differential equation is in the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=f(x)g(y)$ we can try to solve it by separation of variables.

For the equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y^2\sin(x)$, we have:

$\begin{align}
f(x)&=\sin(x)
\\\\
g(y)&=y^2
\end{align}$

Let's separate the variables.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=f(x)g(y)
\\\\
\dfrac{1}{g(y)}\,dy&=f(x)\,dx
\\\\
\dfrac{1}{y^2}\,dy&=\sin(x)\,dx
\\\\
\displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{y^2}\,dy&=\displaystyle \sin(x)\,dx
\end{align}$

Instead of dividing both sides of the equation by $y^2$, Anastasia multiplied on the left side and divided on the right.
In conclusion, step 1 is incorrect. The separation of variables wasn't done correctly.

question.content:
Anastasia tried to solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y^2\sin(x)$. This is her work:

$\begin{align}
&&\dfrac{dy}{dx}&=y^2\sin(x)
\\\\
\text{Step 1:}&&\displaystyle\int y^2\,dy&=\displaystyle\int \sin(x)\,dx
\\\\
\text{Step 2:}&&\dfrac{y^3}{3}&=-\cos(x)+C_1
\\\\
\text{Step 3:}&&y^3&=-3\cos(x)+C
\\\\
\text{Step 4:}&&y&=\sqrt[3]{-3\cos(x)+C}
\end{align}$

**Is Anastasia's work correct? If not, what is her mistake?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: When we multiply both sides of the original equation by $\dfrac{dx}{y^2}$, we should get $\dfrac{1}{y^2}\,dy=\sin(x)\,dx$. Then we would have successfully separated the $x$- and $y$-terms and differentials and would be ready to integrate.

When we multiply both sides of the original equation by $\dfrac{dx}{y^2}$, we should get $\dfrac{1}{y^2}\,dy=\sin(x)\,dx$. Then we would have successfully separated the $x$- and $y$-terms and differentials and would be ready to integrate.
choices.content: **Step 1** is incorrect. The separation of variables wasn't done correctly.

choices.clue:
$\displaystyle \int \sin(x)\,dx=-\cos(x)+C$

Anastasia can subtract the constant from both sides of the equation and still have an arbitrary constant on the right side.
choices.content: **Step 2** is incorrect. Anastasia didn't integrate $\sin(x)$ correctly.

choices.clue: When Anastasia takes the cube root of the left-hand side of the equation, she must take the cube root of the entire right-hand side of the equation, including the constant.
choices.content: **Step 4** is incorrect. The right-hand side of the equation should be $\sqrt[3]{-\cos(x)}+C$.
